name: issue_620_fast_loop_floor_exit_pauses_with_window_open
description: When the fast-loop fan_thermostat_check() stops a non-nat-vent WHF (e.g. min-runtime cycling) because indoor cooled to the comfort floor, a monitored sensor already open must result in a pause, not a silently restored active HVAC mode (Issue #620, Fix C)
notes: UNSUPPORTED (Issue #620): this scenario documents a deliberate scope decision, not a bug
to fix later. It attempts to isolate fan_thermostat_check()'s STOP_COOLED_TO_FLOOR outcome
(the fast, tick-level thermostatic-backstop path fixed by Issue #620 Fix C) in the
simulation harness, and could not be made to reliably exercise that exact path across
several redesigns:
1. use_coordinator=false + a genuine nat-vent session: nat_vent_temperature_check()
(a separate, already-correct comfort-floor implementation, called directly by
_handle_temp_update() before fan_thermostat_check() gets a turn) always intercepts
and exits the session first.
2. use_coordinator=false + a non-nat-vent min-runtime fan (activate_fan_min_runtime),
sensor_open with seed:true: the seed flag is silently ignored in engine-only mode
(see run_production.py's sensor_open handler -- seed only applies when
coordinator is not None), so handle_door_window_open()'s full reactivation logic
runs anyway and converts the fan into a nat-vent session, defeating the setup.
3. use_coordinator=true + seed:true, timed near the real incident's 06:30 timestamp:
the real coordinator's scheduled morning-wakeup trigger fires at that exact time
and, thanks to Fix A (the new _sync_paused_by_door_with_live_sensors() choke-point
check), correctly pauses the sensor BEFORE fan_thermostat_check() ever runs --
masking whether Fix C specifically is doing anything.
4. use_coordinator=true + seed:true, shifted to a neutral afternoon time (no scheduled
trigger nearby): activate_fan_min_runtime produced no observable effect at all in
this harness configuration -- investigation did not converge before time was
allocated to the remaining #620 fixes.
The harness has no direct 'fire the periodic 5-min thermostatic backstop timer with
trigger=timer' event type, which is what actually fires in production (confirmed via the
real incident's own log line: 'Fan thermostat check: trigger=timer'), and building one
was out of scope for this issue's blast radius.
Fix C's correctness instead rests on tests/test_fan_control.py's existing unit-test
coverage for fan_thermostat_check(), which already regression-caught a real defect
during this fix's implementation (an event-type mislabeling for the non-nat-vent case,
test_stops_non_natvent_fan_without_natvent_event) -- direct evidence that suite is
sensitive to exactly this class of change, even without an end-to-end scenario here.

events.note: Afternoon (deliberately away from 06:30 morning-wakeup/bedtime/pre-cool scheduled triggers, which would otherwise pause the sensor via Fix A first and mask Fix C): indoor 70F, outdoor 63F.
Hot day forecast, cool mode wanted -- CA would restore to this mode if the bug were present.
Window already open, seeded silently (no dispatch) -- models a sensor that's been open for a while, matching the real incident. Does not trigger handle_door_window_open()'s reactivation logic.
WHF starts via a min-runtime cycle -- _fan_active=True, _natural_vent_active stays False (not a nat-vent session).

Indoor has cooled to 63.5F -- below the 64F comfort floor, outdoor still below indoor (Check 1's free-cooling-gone condition not met). This temp_update dispatches through the real coordinator listener chain, reaching fan_thermostat_check() (_fan_active=True); its STOP_COOLED_TO_FLOOR outcome must fire here with the window still open.

assertions.reason: The fan stops once indoor reaches the comfort floor either way (pause or restore) -- this just confirms the session actually ended.

Issue #620 Fix C: the comfort-floor exit must route through _exit_nat_vent(), which checks the still-open sensor and pauses (_paused_by_door=True) instead of restoring the classification's cool mode into the open window. Before the fix, _deactivate_fan()'s default restore_hvac=True would have set HVAC to cool@74F here with no sensor check at all.

verdict.summary: A comfort-floor exit with a monitored sensor still open pauses HVAC instead of restoring an active mode (Issue #620, Fix C)
verdict.observed_behavior: min-runtime fan running -> indoor cools to floor with window still open -> paused_by_door=True, HVAC stays off
verdict.expected_behavior: The fast-loop comfort-floor exit checks live sensor state before restoring HVAC, matching the treatment Issue #418 already gave the sibling outdoor-rise exit
